lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: proving the Pythagorean theorem using similarity
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: proving the Pythagorean theorem using similarity

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: A 2 m pole casts a 3 m shadow; a tree casts a 12 m shadow. Tree height?
Why does a line parallel to one side divide the others proportionally?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 6 corresponds to DE = 12. If BC = 8, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 3 and 3. Find the altitude.
A 4 m pole casts a 5 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 15 m shadow. How tall is the building?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The parallel line bisects both sides by definition.
The result follows from the Pythagorean theorem applied twice.
The two parts of each side are congruent because the line is parallel.
The parallel line creates corresponding angles, giving a smaller triangle similar to the original by AA, so the sides are in proportion.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 3 corresponds to DE = 6. If BC = 6, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 2 and 8. Find the altitude.
A 3 m pole casts a 8 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 48 m shadow. How tall is the building?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: The Pythagorean theorem can be proved using similarity. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: Similarity gives a² + b² = c² only for isosceles right triangles.
The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to the original; writing both similarity proportions and adding them yields a² + b² = c².
The theorem follows because all right triangles are similar to each other.
The theorem follows from the triangle inequality.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 7 corresponds to DE = 21. If BC = 4, find EF.
